Definition: probably from a primary verb δίκω (to cast); a seine (for fishing):--net.
BiblicalUsage: A fishing net, the working tool of the first disciples, left at once when Jesus called them to follow Him. Peter let down the net at Jesus' word and caught so many fish it began to break, and after the resurrection the net came up full of a hundred and fifty-three great fishes without tearing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe following Jesus starts with leaving the net behind and ends with a catch I could never haul in alone. The same hands that mended nets were given a new trade, and the net that once fed a family now pictures a kingdom gathering people.
RelatedEvents: The Calling of the First Disciples
